item.description: Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Monday night’s matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings was supposed to be a good one. The Bills have one of the most fascinating offenses in the league, led by quarterback Josh Allen, while the Vikings defense may be the best unit in all of football at the halfway point of the season. Unfortunately for football fans tuning in to ESPN, the matchup did not deliver, with Minnesota quarterback Carson Wentz largely responsible for the game turning into a trainwreck. Wentz, who was stepping in for an injured Kyler Murray, was simply awful. By the end of the night, he had accrued a stat line of 8-for-25 passing for 81 yards and two interceptions, and those atrocious stats don’t even tell the whole story of just how painful the performance was. item.description: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Carson Wentz made his second start of the season for the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football , and the Buffalo Bills left U.S. Bank Stadium with a 23-6 win, dropping the Vikings to 6-2, while Buffalo improved to 7-1. And just like that, Minnesota has fallen to third place in the NFC North. On offense, with Wentz under center, absolutely nothing changed. In fact, the results were even worse than what we witness when Kyler Murray was trying to see over the offensive line in weeks past. Luckily, the Vikings GM Nolan Teasley can still fix what has been ailing this team all season, and that is bad quarterback play. The NFL trade deadline isn’t for another 15 hours, meaning there’s still hope to save a season that, on paper, still looks pretty good. The MN Vikings defense kept them in the game yet again, but Wentz would go on to throw 2 more interceptions, 0 touchdowns and just 81 total yards on 8/25 passing. item.title: James Cook delivered for the Bills on Monday night against the Vikings
item.description: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN named James Cook the player of the game in their postgame show and it’s easy to see why. The Buffalo Bills leaned on their running back against the Minnesota Vikings, and despite a slow start, Cook delivered over the course of the game and scored what felt like the game-ending touchdown with 6:17 left in the fourth quarter. That’s seven straight games with a rushing touchdown for Cook. Cook’s previous career high in carries came in 2025 when he ran the ball 32 times with two offensive lineman injured against a really talented Pittsburgh Steelers defense. The same thing happened in Minnesota, when two Bills offensive linemen were on the shelf and Buffalo needed the help. Cook toted the rock 31 times for 107 yards at a tough 3.5 yards per carry. Cook’s long was only 11 yards on Monday. In the passing game, Cook was targeted once but let the Allen pass go through his hands but he probably wouldn’t have picked up many yards anyway. The rest of the rushing game was shaky at best. Josh Allen ran the ball five times for 16 yards (outside the first half kneel down), mostly on designed runs. Ray Davis had two runs for two yards. Ty Johnson had one rush for one yard. Cook deserves a ton of credit for continuing to grind against the Vikings. It’s a short week for the Blls heading into a Sunday game after a road trip on Monday night, so hopefully he can get iced up with a veteran rest day this week. After the game, Cook was nonchalant on how his body feels. “[I feel] excellent. Feel like I didn’t play a game.” Hopefully he feels that way in the morning.

It ensured they entered the final international window of 2026 in positive spirits. As the club action takes a two-week break, BBC Sport Wales looks at the highs and lows of the Red Dragons' season to date. So how does Wrexham's performance so far this term compare to the same stage last season? What has gone well? Wrexham's performances in the draws with Cardiff City and Watford early on were encouraging. item.title: Warriors' Will Richard hoping that thumb injury won't require surgery
item.description: Golden State Warriors guard Will Richard drives to the basket against Miami Heat guard Klay Thompson on Thursday at Chase Center. (Tony Avelar/Associated Press) If Will Richard can play, he will. In a rough twist of fate for the Golden State Warriors ' second-year wing, Richard's left-thumb ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) tear - as revealed in the team's injury report Sunday night - came on a simple box-out in Saturday's overtime win over Orlando. He thought he'd just jammed the thumb. But this was a full and not partial UCL tear, as Richard told reporters pregame Monday, and suddenly the complexion of the 23-year-old's season had shifted. Conventional wisdom, given such a full tear, might suggest immediate corrective surgery. Not so fast. "We're trying to wait until the swelling goes down," Richard said Monday, while squeezing a red grip device in his left hand. "Do a workout, catching, going full speed and all that, see if it's comfortable. "But if I feel comfortable and confident, I want to play," he continued. "I want to be out there for the guys." There are two typical paths in the event of a UCL tear in the thumb, said Dr. David Hay, an orthopedic surgeon and hand and wrist specialist in Los Angeles. If the joint remains stable, an athlete could return to play as soon as swelling decreases and a capable external stabilizer is found. If the joint is deemed unstable, though, the most obvious path is surgery, which - utilizing what's called "suture augmentation" - could get Richard back to playing within four to six weeks, Hay said. If Richard does decide on surgery, then, he could be off the floor until well into December. The 2025 second-round pick had established himself as an early-season member of head coach Steve Kerr 's rotation, averaging 5.1 points in 17.2 minutes per game and serving as a key defensive option off the bench. "I mean, that's an area on our team that we need to improve on is at the point of attack, and being able to guard those guys that are the main for the other team," Richard told the Chronicle in late October. "So, I feel like that's just my focus." Richard will likely find an answer to his decision on surgery by sometime next week, he said. If he goes under the knife and misses extended time, the Warriors will need consistent minutes from 33-year-old defensive stopper Gary Payton II, who also missed Monday's game against the Pelicans with knee inflammation. item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Rory McIlroy can still secure a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, but the window is closing fast. He sits 533.93 points behind leader Eugenio Chacarra with just one tournament left on the schedule. A victory at the DP World Tour Championship starting Thursday, Nov. 12, guarantees the trophy for the Northern Irishman regardless of where Chacarra finishes. This is the only path that secures the win without needing help from others. The math gets much harder if McIlroy finishes second or lower. McIlroy finished third last week in Abu Dhabi to cut the lead almost in half, but the gap remains significant. Patrick Reed sits in third place, a further 181 points back, and could still complicate the standings if he wins. The Chacarra Factor Eugenio Chacarra holds the advantage because he controls his own destiny. The 26-year-old Spaniard has won three times this season and needs only a victory in Dubai to guarantee the title. He faces a direct fight with McIlroy, who has dominated this race for the past 15 years. Chacarra knows the challenge he faces against the veteran. item.title: Bam Adebayo given blunt ‘Joel Embiid’ reality check by Miami Heat legend Udonis Haslem
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Udonis Haslem has delivered a blunt message to Bam Adebayo, urging the Miami Heat star to embrace his own strengths rather than try to play like Joel Embiid. Haslem believes Adebayo has the talent to produce 30-point performances but must bring the effort and energy required to reach that level consistently. The former Heat captain shared his assessment of the centre in comments posted by @wynetwork, using Embiid as an example of a different type of offensive player. Udonis Haslem tells Bam Adebayo to embrace his strengths instead of copying Joel Embiid Haslem made his point clear when discussing the expectations surrounding Adebayo, who he believes has All-Star ability but needs to approach the game in his own way. “You’re an effort and energy guy, that has All Star talent. You’re not Joel Embiid,” Haslem said, according to the quote shared by @wynetwork . “Joel Embiid can go out there on one knee and get 30.” The comparison was not intended to dismiss Adebayo’s scoring ability. Instead, Haslem was highlighting the different qualities that make the two centres effective. He believes Adebayo can reach the same scoring mark, but his route to doing so requires a consistent level of activity and intensity. “You can get your 30, but you have to bring that s*** every night to get your 30,” Haslem said. “That’s who you are. And that’s ok to be that guy.” There is also some history behind Haslem’s comments. The former Miami captain shared a locker room with Adebayo before retiring and has been part of his development into one of the Heat’s leading players. item.title: Bills defense turns tables on Vikings in victory
item.description: Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen skips away from Minnesota's Andrew van Ginkel as the Bills claim a hard-fought win over the Vikings (David Berding) The Buffalo Bills turned the tables on the Minnesota Vikings on Monday, producing a steely defensive performance on the road to grab a 23-6 victory in Minneapolis. A low-scoring showdown between the Bills' potent offense and the stingiest defense in the NFL ended with a hard-fought Buffalo victory at the US Bank Stadium. Buffalo's defense proved decisive in the win, restricting the Vikings to just two field goals on a miserable night for Minnesota quarterback Carson Wentz. Veteran back-up Wentz, starting in place of the injured Kyler Murray, struggled throughout, tossing two interceptions, coughing up a fumble and recording just eight completions. The Bills offense dug deep to grind out victory, with running back James Cook rushing for 107 yards from 31 carries. Bills quarterback Josh Allen threw 234 yards with one touchdown from 21 completions. "It's exactly what it was -- a great performance," Allen told ESPN. "We knew that it was going to take all four quarters. "That's a great team that we just played. They're extremely well coach and that defense is the best in the league for a reason. "We kept grinding, kind of wore them down in the fourth quarter. Our defense played fantastic." Buffalo improved to 7-1 with the win to tighten their grip on the AFC East, ahead of the second-placed New England Patriots (5-4). The Vikings fell to 6-2 in the NFC North. An attritional first half saw Buffalo kicker Tyler Bass open the scoring with a 39-yard field goal in the first quarter before Vikings counterpart Will Reichard level with a 43-yard effort in the second quarter. Buffalo grabbed the first touchdown of the game in the final minute of the second quarter, with Allen leading an eight-play 80-yard drive before finding Keleki Latu with a 25-yard touchdown pass to make it 10-3. Reichard narrowed the deficit to four points with a field goal in the final seconds of the first half, but Minnesota failed to add to their tally thereafter. Instead the Bills steadily built on their lead, with Bass scoring a 25-yard field goal to make it 13-6 midway through the third quarter. Cook then struck the decisive blow in the fourth quarter, barreling over from five yards to cap a 15-play, 84-yard drive that took 8min 32sec off the clock. item.title: ‘Completely Washed,’ ‘Get Him Off My Team’ — James Harden Gets Shredded Over ‘Pathetic’ Defensive Sequence vs. Shorthanded Hornets
item.description: 'Completely Washed,' 'Get Him Off My Team' — James Harden Gets Shredded Over 'Pathetic' Defensive Sequence vs. Shorthanded Hornets James Harden came under fire for his lack of defensive effort during a rough third-quarter sequence in the Cleveland Cavaliers’ 124-112 road loss to the undermanned Charlotte Hornets on Monday. Harden displayed next to no urgency as Charlotte grabbed two offensive rebounds on the same possession before the 37-year-old finally got involved by fouling Grayson Allen. The defensive lapse came against a Hornets team missing three starters, yet Charlotte still snapped a six-game losing streak after leading by as many as 33 points. The NBA world promptly piled on the 2018 MVP, adding to the scrutiny surrounding his start to Year 18. James Harden’s Lackluster Defense Draws Concerns and Backlash With Charlotte leading 80-64 and looking to extend its third-quarter edge, Allen fired a corner triple, which missed the mark. Ryan Kalkbrenner secured the offensive rebound and found Sion James open beyond the arc. All the while, Harden stayed underneath the basket, making almost no effort to box out before opting not to contest James’ shot. The sophomore guard’s shot was also off target, with Allen taking notice and crashing the boards over Harden. The sharpshooter drew a foul on the offensive rebound, converting both free throws to put the Hornets up 82-64 with 8:29 left in the quarter. Legion Hoops shared the troubling sequence, drawing attention to Harden’s lack of hustle with a simple “yikes.” Rebounding was already a sore spot. After Saturday’s 109-97 home loss to the New York Knicks, Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson said, “We’ve got to find a way to rebound better collectively.” Two nights later, Charlotte won the battle of the boards 49-32 and grabbed 17 offensive rebounds to Cleveland’s 4. Kalkbrenner had 10 of them on his way to 15 rebounds overall. READ MORE: ‘We Keep On Having Bad Habits’ — Giannis Antetokounmpo Makes Feelings Clear on Miami Heat’s Dismal Start to NBA Season The Hornets won the third quarter 38-27 behind a 16-0 run that stretched their lead to 100-67, and Allen finished with a game-high 27 points. Meanwhile, Harden recorded just 11 points on 3-for-9 shooting (33.3%), including 2-for-7 from deep (28.6%), with 3 rebounds, 5 assists, 1 steal, and 4 turnovers in 25 minutes. The 11-time All-Star had his moments, including a 4-point play earlier in the third, but posted a minus-22 plus-minus, the second-worst mark on his team. item.title: Seton Hall basketball beats Charlotte -- and finds a point guard
item.description: PHILADELPHIA – The Seton Hall basketball did more than win a game Monday night against a decent Charlotte team. The Pirates found a point guard. Junior Mihailo Petrovic came off the bench to spark an offense that had been stagnant through the season’s early going. The transfer from Illinois pushed all the right buttons as the Hall prevailed 68-62 before a small but vocal Pirate-dominated crowd at the Palestra, appropriately known as the cathedral of college basketball. Petrovic finished with 12 points, six assists, three steals and two turnovers in 30 minutes. He shot 4-of-6 from the field and it was clear his teammates’ confidence clearly rose with him at the controls. The ball moved better, the floor was spaced better, and the pick-and-roll consistently worked. In the ultimate compliment, Hall coach Shaheen Holloway started Petrovic in the second half over Del Jones – something the coach rarely does. It was recognition that he’s found something – if you have a point guard, you have a chance. And Seton Hall (3-0) now has a chance. Charlotte 49ers (2-1) was picked to finish fifth in the 13-team American Athletic Conference. There’s a chance this holds up as a Quad 2 victory and a neutral-court resume-booster. FIVE TAKEAWAYS 1. Devin Williams breaks out Terry Copeland’s foul trouble opened the door for Devin Williams, and the 6-foot-10 junior played his best game thus far, notching 16 points, four assists and two blocks in 22 minutes. Williams ran some nice pick-and-roll action and did a nice job drawing defenders to the paint before dishing to open teammates. He also set solid screens. He wasn’t perfect – he takes too many jump shots and should use his length to rebound better – but it was a clear step forward for the Florida Atlantic transfer. 2. So, why does the energy around Minnesota feel so dark right now? It's hard to win without a quarterback, and the Vikings looked Monday night like a team without a quarterback in a 23-6 loss. Carson Wentz was abysmal in place of an injured Kyler Murray, who has struggled himself when on the field this season. The trade deadline looms on Tuesday, and pressure is mounting on the Vikings to make a move at quarterback to avoid wasting a stellar defense. Here's a look at whether a trade is realistic. LIVE: Follow latest NFL trade rumors, updates Will Vikings trade for a QB? The Vikings cannot go on with Wentz as their quarterback. That much is clear after Monday's loss, even if he was playing through pain. The good news is they won't have to, at least in the long run, as Murray is considered week-to-week with a hamstring injury and isn't dealing with an injury serious enough to necessitate a stint on injured reserve. The bad news is that Murray simply hasn't been much better. The former No. 1 pick has only one multi-touchdown game this season, and he hasn't thrown for 250 yards in any of his five full games. The offense had more success with Murray than it did with Wentz on Monday, but the bar set by Wentz was remarkably low. Max Brosmer also looked solid after replacing Wentz in garbage time on Monday, but he hasn't proven that he can sustain the kind of play that can win games for Minnesota. The possibility of a trade has to be considered very real. The Vikings didn't just find out Monday night that they have a quarterback problem, so they aren't starting from scratch, but there has to be an increased sense of urgency. With such a dominant defense, the Vikings don't have to bring in a star to give themselves a chance to win. Kirk Cousins and Daniel Jones, both former Vikings, reportedly won't be traded, but would a strong Minnesota offer change that? The Commanders love super-sub Marcus Mariota, but would he be available with the season likely lost in Washington?
